kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-05.title: Step back one day at a time
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-05.body:
Tomorrow is Tuesday, so today is Monday. Yesterday is the day before Monday: Sunday.

**Answer: (A) Sunday**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-05.title: Two days back
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-05.body:
Yesterday is 2 days before tomorrow. Two days before Tuesday: Monday, then Sunday.

**Answer: (A) Sunday**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-06.title: Two parts of the rectangle
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-06.body:
The part of the rectangle that is outside the triangle has two pieces:

- the top piece, above the triangle: 6 orange flowers;
- the bottom piece, below the triangle: 3 blue flowers.

$6 + 3 = 9$ flowers.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-06.title: Cross out
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-06.body:
Look only at the flowers inside the green rectangle and cross out those that are also inside the blue triangle. 9 flowers are left: 6 at the top and 3 at the bottom.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-07.title: Add, then take away
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-07.body:
The four dice show $4 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 10$ dots. The fifth die must show $15 - 10 = 5$.

**Answer: (E) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-07.title: Count on
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-07.body:
Start at 10 (the four dice) and count up to 15: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 — that is 5 more.

**Answer: (E) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-08.title: Look up each letter
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-08.body:
From the table: R → \*, A → %, N → #, G → \$, O → +.

So RANGO is \* % # \$ +.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-08.title: Rule out quickly
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-08.body:
A is %, so the second sign must be %: that leaves (B) and (C). N is # and comes before G (\$), so it is (B).

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-09.title: Start at the cheese
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-09.body:
All five gates are around the cheese. Follow the corridors behind gates 1, 2 and 3 with your finger: they only lead to dead ends, so the mouse can never get to them. The mouse's corridors come down to gate 4 and to gate 5. Close these two and the cheese is safe.

**Answer: (E) 4 and 5**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-09.title: Start at the mouse
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-09.body:
Trace the paths starting at the mouse. Every path that gets near the cheese ends at gate 4 or at gate 5. So both of these gates must be closed.

**Answer: (E) 4 and 5**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-13.title: Half and 8 more
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-13.body:
The cows are half of the sheep, so the sheep are the cows twice. The sheep are also the cows plus 8. So 8 must be one 'cow group': there are 8 cows and $8 + 8 = 16$ sheep.

Total: $8 + 16 = 24$ animals.

**Answer: (D) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-13.title: Try numbers
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-13.body:
Try 8 cows: then there are 16 sheep, and 8 is half of 16. ✓ (With 6 cows: 14 sheep, but 6 is not half of 14.) So $8 + 16 = 24$.

**Answer: (D) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-15.title: Try the biggest squares
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-15.body:
The biggest numbers are at the bottom right.

- 14, 15, 19, 20: sum 68 > 63 ✓
- 13, 14, 18, 19: sum 64 > 63 ✓
- 12, 13, 17, 18: sum 60 — too small. All other squares are even smaller.

So Peter chose one of the two good squares. Both contain 14 (and 19).

**Answer: (A) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-15.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-15.body:
15 and 20 are missing from the square 13, 14, 18, 19; 17 and 18 are missing from the square 14, 15, 19, 20. Only 14 is in both good squares.

**Answer: (A) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-16.title: Work backwards
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-16.body:
At the end Tree 1 has 5 sparrows.

- Before 4 sparrows came back, Tree 1 had $5 - 4 = 1$.
- Before 7 sparrows flew away, Tree 1 had $1 + 7 = 8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-16.title: Net change
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-16.body:
Tree 1 lost 7 and got back 4, so it lost 3 sparrows in total. It ended with 5, so it started with $5 + 3 = 8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-17.title: Compare with Adam
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-17.body:
Lucy is 7 years older than Adam. Monica is 8 years older than Adam. So Monica is the oldest, then Lucy, then Adam.

**Answer: (E) Monica, Lucy, Adam**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-17.title: Pick an age
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-17.body:
Say Adam is 1. Then Lucy is 8 and Monica is 9. Oldest to youngest: Monica, Lucy, Adam.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-18.title: How much each change adds
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-18.body:
Changing a red token: 1 token becomes 3, so she gets 2 more tokens. Changing a white token: 1 becomes 2, so 1 more token.

To end with few tokens she should change white tokens. She has only 1 white token. After changing it she has only red tokens, so the second change must be a red one (which gives 3 white). The third change can be a white one again.

$4 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 8$ tokens.

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-18.title: Try it out
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0102-18.body:
Start: 3 red, 1 white (4 tokens).

1. White → 2 red: 5 red (5 tokens).
2. Red → 3 white: 4 red, 3 white (7 tokens).
3. White → 2 red: 6 red, 2 white (8 tokens).

Three white changes are impossible: after the first one she has no white token left. Using two red changes gives at least $4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 9$. So 8 is the smallest.

**Answer: (C) 8**
